column1: # The deletion gates of SPEC.md §8, as cases both ends have to decide the same way.
# This is the one decision made on the phone that can destroy something, so it is written down
# once and checked against both implementations rather than trusted to two readings of the same
# paragraph. The Rust simulator's phone and the Kotlin session module each run every line.
# Columns, tab separated:
#   name              what the case is
#   origin            this-transfer | earlier — which gate §8 demands
#   candidate_size    the size the desktop stated
#   candidate_mtime   the time the desktop stated
#   vault_content     the bytes the desktop verified; its sha256 is the expected digest
#   local_present     yes | no — whether the phone still has the file
#   local_mtime       the time the phone's copy carries
#   local_content     the bytes the phone holds now
#   expect            deleted | kept-changed | failed
# A case that is kept is never a failure of the protocol: §8's whole failure analysis is that
# desktop state, however stale or forged, can cause under-deletion and never a wrong deletion.

committed this session and untouched
